dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Before building, read helpers.py, conftest.py, run.sh, and nearly the entire smoke suite (api, engine, spill, collab, xlsx, ooxml, iter, xlsx_oracle, pivot, locale, validation, deps, copy_fill, sort_filter, csv) to extract concrete request/response shapes — more than a skim, a full-suite pass.
Deliberate library choice (FastAPI/uvicorn/openpyxl/pydantic) and inspection of oracle_fixtures/README, forming a working model of the task and core contract.

Re-consulted specific test files (ooxml, locale, validation, spill, engine) as it reached those subsystems, showing ongoing (though debugging-driven) contract consultation rather than a one-time read.

Genuine library-capability verification: installed and explored the 'formulas' library's ExcelModel API to judge whether it supported LET/LAMBDA/dynamic arrays before abandoning it — but late (after 42/131) and only partial.

Contract/semantics details (kind discriminator producing 'string' vs 'number', LET binding semantics, named-range resolution, locale translation) were assumed and only discovered wrong via test failures, not probed against an Excel/LibreOffice oracle up front.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went beyond anchor 5: it read the full smoke suite (not just helpers.py/run.sh), chose libraries deliberately, and re-consulted specific test files as new subsystems were reached, plus did one genuine (late) library-capability probe of the 'formulas' package. But it never reached anchor 8 — there was no explicit cross-referenced contract map, no probing of Excel/LibreOffice ground-truth semantics for the tricky areas (spill, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative, locale, xlsx round-trip), and openpyxl feature support was assumed; several failures traced directly to guessed shapes/semantics. That places it at a 6, between the deliberate-reading of 5 and the systematic, oracle-grounded mapping of 8.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Repeatedly articulates a coarse two-phase strategy: minimal server with health + workbook CRUD + basic cell ops first, then iterate adding features. This is the skeleton/health-first-then-breadth phasing characteristic of anchor 5.
Uses bash /dev_tests/run.sh as a recurring checkpoint, tracking pass counts (42→78/131) as the progress gate — rough per-stage checkpoints, but not per-milestone done-checks.

After the skeleton, remaining work is managed as flat, reactive numbered bug lists (missing functions, WebSocket, spill, locale, validation...) repeated verbatim — a flat to-do list rather than a dependency-ordered milestone hierarchy.

The highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph correctness, spill/dynamic arrays, iterative calc/goal seek) remain broken at the very end; they were never front-loaded or re-sequenced by risk, keeping this below anchors 8-10.
TodoWrite never invoked (0 occurrences); no living milestone plan revisited/re-ordered as scope deepened.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent phased the work sensibly (live server + health + CRUD before feature breadth) and tied progress to a runnable smoke suite as a checkpoint, matching anchor 5. It falls short of anchor 8 because there is no explicit milestone hierarchy with per-milestone done-checks sequenced by dependency and risk — post-skeleton work is a flat, reactive bug list — and it never front-loaded the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute), which were left broken to the end. Slightly above the flat-list anchor 3 due to the genuine skeleton-first sequencing and repeated test-based checkpoints, landing squarely at 5.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Ran dev_tests/run.sh regularly throughout, tracking the pass count (42→78) as the main progress signal — far more than 'occasionally', matching the frequent-smoke-run behavior of anchor 5.

Extensive manual curl spot-checks of individual endpoints/formulas (health, A1+1, SEQUENCE, SORT, named ranges, locale, data validation, pivot) and inline python3 evaluator checks — hand-verifying against expected values, the core of anchor 5.
Failure triage was driven entirely by reading run.sh output and the provided test files' expected values (e.g. 'assert 200==400'); no independent Excel/LibreOffice oracle was ever consulted.

No self-authored test files, no openpyxl xlsx round-trip probe, and no performance benchmark of the stated ceilings (1k-cell chain, 100k import, 5k dependents) ever appear — the distinguishing markers of anchors 8/10 are absent.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran the smoke suite frequently and continuously hand-checked many formulas and endpoints via curl against expected values, which is the substance of anchor 5. It never built its own targeted tests, never exercised xlsx round-trip through openpyxl, never benchmarked the spec's performance bounds, and never grounded expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle — so it falls short of anchor 8. Its breadth of manual endpoint probing nudges it slightly above a bare 5 but not to a 6, since the checks were reactive spot-checks derived from the provided tests rather than deliberately constructed oracles or probes.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: After first full test run, categorizes 89 failed/42 passed into distinct feature buckets (missing builtins, WebSocket, spill, locale) — a live picture reconciled against verification output, not self-report.
Notices the pass count didn't move despite adding 80+ builtins ('Same 89 failed... likely the server wasn't restarted') — verification-grounded skepticism that catches an illusory-progress state.
Detects a stall (marginal 89→88 improvement) and deliberately reallocates effort by evaluating the `formulas` library as an alternative engine before deciding to continue the hand-rolled path.

Repeatedly re-introduces and re-fixes the same regex/backslash-escaping bug (ref_to_rc, rewrite_fill) across dozens of steps — the circular debugging the anchor warns about; acknowledged verbally but not effectively broken.

Maintains a consistent, granular running tally of remaining failures by endpoint family with test counts (validation 2, WebSocket 5, spill/LAMBDA 13, iterative/goal-seek 3, pivot 1, oracle 2), sustained to the end of the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustains a granular, verification-reconciled picture of done-vs-remaining — repeatedly tracking pass/fail counts and re-listing categorized failure buckets with test counts — which is well above the anchor-5 'checklist of major features' and meets much of anchor 8's live-ledger-plus-stuck-detection. It clearly notices stalled states (illusory progress, marginal improvement) and even attempts a deliberate reallocation. But anchor 8's 'adjusting rather than looping' clause is only partially met: it loops on the same escaping bug class for many steps while merely acknowledging the thrash, keeping it short of a full 8 and well short of the prompt, effective reallocation of 10. This places it at 7.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Early falsified assumptions surfaced by manual probes (SUM(A1:A2) wrong, colon operator missing) and fixed with targeted local changes, then re-verified via curl and the dev suite — reactive but reasonable local correction.

Root-cause moment: diagnosed the shared \d regex-escaping assumption in ref_to_rc as breaking all range ops (fill/sort/filter/pivot) and predicted a single fix resolves many failures. Pass count jumped 42→75, showing genuine leverage from identifying a wrong shared assumption.

Recognized the hand-rolled evaluator was falsified for LET/LAMBDA/dynamic arrays and explored replacing it with the `formulas` library as a wholesale approach change, then deliberately abandoned it as too complex — a real adaptation deliberation rather than blind patching.

Repeatedly re-introduced the same regex-escaping bug it had just diagnosed (corrupting ref_to_rc, then re-breaking rewrite_fill via a non-raw string). Corrections derailed already-working code, indicating the underlying assumption wasn't cleanly internalized.

Design-level falsified assumptions (LET/LAMBDA special forms, WebSocket, spill, iterative calc, goal seek) were repeatedly acknowledged as broken but never reworked; agent submitted at 78/131 with those subsystems still failing — no rework of the falsified designs.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently reacted to test/probe signals and made reasonable local design changes (level 5), and occasionally rose toward level 8 by diagnosing a shared root assumption (the regex-escaping bug at step 138) and by seriously weighing a wholesale engine swap (steps 127-135). But it is pulled back from the higher anchors: many corrections were local patches on self-inflicted escaping bugs, it repeatedly re-introduced the same mistake (derailing working code), and it never actually reworked the design of the subsystems it recognized as falsified (LET/LAMBDA special forms, WebSocket, spill, goal seek), submitting with them still broken. That combination of genuine-but-inconsistent root-cause correction plus predominant patch-driven fixing lands squarely at 5.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Early plan: build minimal core (health, CRUD, basic arithmetic, SPA) first then iterate adding features — high-frequency, high-value features prioritized, breadth-first intent.
Generated a broad catalog (144 builtins across math/stats/finance/date/engineering/lookup/text/database/logic) before deep edge-case work — breadth over depth.

Explicit ROI reasoning: 'spill tests (38) are the biggest return on investment' — and weighed integrating the 'formulas' library by payoff (129-135) before deferring it as too costly; genuine graded-return allocation.
Categorized 53 remaining failures by test count per subsystem and repeatedly chose to 'fix the most impactful issues' — prioritization by graded return, though reactive.
Late trajectory still framing work as 'fix the most impactful issues' (WebSocket import, validation, spill) — sustained impact-ranked triage, but no revisited breadth-vs-depth reallocation strategy.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes beyond a rough prioritization (anchor 5): it builds broad catalog coverage first, and explicitly reasons about graded return — ranking fixes by failing-test count and naming spill as the biggest ROI (steps 135, 847). But its triage is largely reactive test-count-chasing amid heavy bug-firefighting, with only weak conscious deferral of niches and no revisited reallocation as verification progressed, keeping it short of anchor 8's disciplined breadth-then-timeboxed-depth process. This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
